An object therefore floats if, for the same volume, it weighs less than the liquid.

He is thought to have taught at the Mouseion, the learned centre that housed the Library. To date him, scholars use a lunar eclipse given as an example in his Dioptra: in 1938, Otto Neugebauer showed that it best matches the one of AD 62. But Hero does not say he observed it: the clue remains fragile.

For him, wars of conquest were nothing but robbery and murder on a grand scale.

According to one account, the caliph al-Hakim summoned him to regulate the floods of the Nile. He drew a dam near the site of the present Aswan Dam, then realised in the field that the project was impossible. To avoid the caliph's anger, he feigned madness.

For him, a projectile moves forward because the thrower impressed on it an immaterial kinetic force, not because the air pushes it. This force runs out by itself, and forced motion then gives way to natural motion: the stone falls back.

Philopon : une force imprimée au project: Philoponus: a force impressed on the projectile, which runs out; two weights dropped arrive almost together.

Au XIIe siècle, Abu'l-Barakat al-Baghdad: In the 12th century, Abu'l-Barakat al-Baghdadi spoke of a "violent inclination" that dies out by itself as the body moves away from the mover. Hipparque, Avicenne (le mayl), Abu'l-Bar: Hipparchus, Avicenna (the mayl), Abu'l-Barakat, then Albert of Saxony and Oresme: the force of the throw passes into the body.
